title: Periplus pack manifest
description: pack.yaml, one per pack directory. Holds the pack's identity, where having two answers is a conflict rather than a merge. Everything else in a pack is a contributed file and merges additively.

$schema.description: The contract this manifest is written against, by the `$id` of the schema above. Allowed here because the top level refuses every key it does not declare, so a file carrying the key an editor reads would otherwise be invalid for saying which rules it follows. What the key claims is which contract the file was authored against; it does not claim that anything resolves the URL today.

depends.description: Zero or more packs, forming a directed acyclic graph rather than a chain: Next.js sits on React and on the Node runtime at once. Because a graph has no single load order, contributions must merge additively and without depending on order. There are no kinds of pack — a root is one with nothing beneath it, and it need not be a language.

detect.description: How a repository is recognised as needing this pack, so `periplus init` can prefill a pin the person then edits. Declared here and never in engine code: a third-party pack is detected exactly as a bundled one is, which is what makes a new stack a pack rather than a release. A pack that declares no detector is never suggested — owning an extension is not the same as being a stack anybody pins, and a language pack firing on every file with its extension would prefill noise into every settings file there is.

any_of.description: The alternatives, tried in the order written. A repository is Drupal if its composer.json requires Drupal core OR it has a docroot, so the block names its combining rule rather than leaving a bare list for a reader to guess at. An empty list detects nothing and is refused here, where the author sees it, rather than at the one call site that would notice.

items.description: One alternative: a repository-relative path that must exist as a file, and optionally a literal substring of that file's text. `contains` is a substring and not a regular expression, because detection reads third-party pack data with no time limit around it and a substring has no backtracking cost. The path stays under the repository root — a signal that leaves it never fires, since a detector that reads outside the checkout turns a committed settings file into a readout of the machine that ran `init`. Both levels are closed: an author who writes `contain:` gets a refusal, not a detector that silently degrades to an existence check and fires on every repository in the language.

grammar.description: Only a pack that owns a language declares this. A domain pack gets its grammars by depending on packs that own them, because a domain pack owning a language means every domain pack touching that language redeclares it and they drift.

format.description: The data format a type read as data is written in, by the name of one of the engine's data readers: yaml. Required with reader data and refused with any other reader. The short form extensions is read as yaml.

relative_to.description: A folder name: the pattern is searched in the path below the deepest directory of that folder that holds the file, and the value is absent for a file no directory of it holds. A folder whose value holds ** is refused at load.

path_values.description: Values computed once per file of this type from its path from the project folder, forward slashes: the pattern is searched there and the template is filled from its named captures and the project's settings values, then normalize and case reshape it; a template naming a name that is neither, or both, is refused. A pattern that does not match leaves the value absent. Every rule on a file of this type may name the value in a template.

sections.description: Spans of the file's text a text rule does not read unless its match names the section under reads_sections. Found in one pass from the start: the earliest opening wins, the first listed on a tie, and the section runs to the end of the first closing match after it, or to the end of the file. In close, a braced name stands for the text the named capture of open matched, escaped.

spans.description: Regions of the file's text a text rule's value reads with from: {enclosing: <name>, capture: <capture>}. A span starts at each match of open outside the sections. From the end of that match, each balance[0] outside the sections counts one up and each balance[1] one down; the span ends after the closing character that brings the count to zero or below, or at the end of the file. Spans of one name nest.

resolve.description: The resolution steps an edge end of a text rule on a file of this type takes when the end declares none: see resolveStep in the pack file schema.

separator.description: The separator beside the file type's resolve.

types.description: Each file type by name. An ending is matched against the end of a file name after a dot, with or without its own leading dot, and the longest ending any loaded pack claims wins; a whole file name claims a file without an ending. The reader says how a rule reads the file: data, text, or tree, which needs the pack's grammar. The short form extensions is one type named by each listed ending, read as a tree when the pack pins a grammar and as data otherwise.

files.description: Exclude is not boundary. A boundary file is unread but the things inside it can still be nodes, because first-party code names them. An excluded file does not exist as far as the map is concerned, not even as the target of a reference, and it is enforced at file selection before anything parses.

folders.description: Named folders a rule refers to with `in:`. A rule never writes a path. The value is a default; the project settings file overrides it for one repository without touching a rule. A value may reference another folder in braces, because a module's own config lives inside whatever custom_module resolves to.

identity.description: How this language composes a qualified name, folds case, and what it must never normalise. Shape not yet derived from enough packs to close.

call_arguments.description: The tree field of a call that holds its arguments, read by an id or a reference end from {argument: N}. Default: arguments.

call_argument.description: The tree node type that holds one argument of a call; its value is its last named child. Without it, each named child of the arguments field is one argument, a comment or other extra node left out.

call_argument_name.description: The field of an argument that holds its name. A named argument is found by its name, not its position, and its value is its last named child.

call_literals.description: The tree node types of a call argument's text literal. Without them, no argument is a text literal.

call_literal_content.description: The tree node types of a text literal's text. A literal with a named child of any other type is not a text literal.

call_literal_delimiters.description: The tree node types of a text literal's named children that are skipped, such as a quote the grammar names.

boundary.description: Path-based, so it needs no pack and works for a dependency published tomorrow. A boundary node enters the map because first-party code refers to it, never because a pack knows about it — otherwise every map on every site carries the same few hundred framework interfaces whether or not anything touches them.

exactVersion.description: Exact, never a range. Grammar node type names carry no stability guarantee across a minor release, so a range lets a rule that matched yesterday match nothing today, silently.

hierarchyEntry.description: What a pack knows about types it does not read. A custom entity almost never writes `implements EntityInterface`; it writes `extends ContentEntityBase`, and the interface is two hops up inside the framework. A rule matching the written clause would match nothing real.
